messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@medstream.health>, Ashok Patel <ashok.patel@medstream.health>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: stakeholder map & procurement pathway (SLA / discount ask)

Hi Claire / Ashok — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Economic buyer: Claire (confirmed) — priority is predictable unit economics and an SLA for 99.9% token availability.
- Technical buyer: Ashok — will own integration and security gating (SOC2 scope, data residency question).
- Procurement: procurement@medstream.health will drive PO and contract redlines, typical 30–45 day cadence.
- Decision criteria: latency (p95), cost per token, auditability (request trace logs), and compliance (SOC2 + data isolation).

Open asks from your side (per call):
1) Procurement wants a redline-friendly SOW and standard DPA; they asked if we can accept a 90-day SLA exception in pilot.
2) Security requested a short questionnaire and an exportable audit log sample.
3) Q: Will Redwood accept a one-time onboarding discount for a 12-month committed pilot? If so, what range?

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send a mutual action plan with milestones (PO, SOW, trial start).
- I’m looping in our legal and revenue ops to confirm whether we can offer a short-term SLA variance and a pilot discount.
- Can procurement share target start and PO lead time?

Attached: MedStream_SOW_v1.pdf (draft) and security_q_2026.xlsx (your requested questionnaire template — we filled the sections we can).

If that matches your notes, I’ll push internal approvals and come back with a commercial/contract path by EOD Thursday.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Lauren / Marcus — forwarding the MedStream thread. Procurement is asking for (a) a short-term SLA variance for pilot and (b) a one-time onboarding discount for a 12-month pilot commit. 

Summary of ask: 
- SLA: pilot wants 99.9% availability target in writing; procurement may ask we accept a 90-day SLA variance for the initial production milestone.
- Discount: they’re expecting a credit in the range of 10–18% as an onboarding incentive.

Why I’m asking: MedStream is a strategic healthcare integration (large footprint across US hospitals). This pilot could expand quickly if latency and cost meet their threshold. I’d like to propose we offer up to 12% onboarding credit without exec approval, cap the pilot SLA deviation to 60 days (if needed), and require Marcus to sign off on security exceptions. 

Can you confirm quickly: 1) floor / ceiling for discount approval by manager; 2) whether SLA deviations require revenue/legal sign-off; 3) anything else I should surface to procurement to speed PO?

Thanks — aiming to respond to Claire by EOD Thursday (12/16).

Ben

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap: stakeholder map & procurement pathway (SLA / discount ask) — approval request

Ben — thanks for the context. Quick responses: 

1) Discount authority: you have approval to offer up to 12% one-time onboarding credit for a signed 12-month pilot. Anything above 12% requires RevOps director sign-off (I can route if needed).

2) SLA variance: we can accept an SLA variance for pilot up to 60 days operationally, but any SLA language that materially changes liability or uptime credits must be approved by Legal. Please flag the specific clause if procurement proposes alternative language.

3) Speeding PO: ensure procurement has a clean SOW, state data residency controls, and include a mutual action plan with deadlines — that often shortens PO cycles.

Loop Marcus for security sign-off on any SOC2 carve-outs. If Marcus can’t clear the carve, we should offer compensating controls (e.g., audit log exports, stricter RBAC).

Approving now — proceed with up to 12% and the 60-day SLA variance contingent on Marcus’s security clearance.

Lauren Bishop

Thanks — I reviewed the security_q_2026.xlsx that Ben attached. High level: 

- No hard stop on SOC2 scope; we need to confirm which control families MedStream requires. If they demand encryption-in-transit + at-rest across on-prem connectors we can meet that, but their ask for full log-forwarding into their SIEM might require an integration effort (estimated 2–3 weeks).
- Compensating controls we can offer immediately: daily audit log export, RBAC scoping for pilot, restricted access to raw PII exports.

For the SLA variance: I’m comfortable with a 60-day operational SLA variance for pilot only provided we put the following in writing: (a) variance is timeboxed to pilot start + 60 days, (b) Redwood commits to remediation plan with milestones if availability drops below agreed thresholds, (c) no change to overall liability caps.

I attached a redlined security worksheet (security_q_2026.xlsx — see tab: marcus_comments). I’ll sign off on SLA variance if procurement accepts compensating controls above.

Marcus Lin
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
